info.title: Kirora API
info.description: The Kirora API: contacts, events, campaigns, journeys and transactional messages over email and push.

tags.name: contacts
tags.description: A contact is one person you can message, with their profile, custom attributes, consent on each channel and topic choices. `identify` creates or updates a contact by your `externalId`, then email, then phone, so use it for every sync rather than looking contacts up by id first. Being on a list or in a segment is not consent: marketing reaches a contact only with consent on its channel. A contact's own records sit under it too: its lists, segments, topic choices, events, journeys, messages and push installations, each a device or browser registered by your own stable `externalInstallationId`. See [IDs and identity](/docs/api/identifiers).

tags.name: events
tags.description: An event is something a contact did, such as `Order Completed`, with properties describing it. Events start journeys, feed segment rules and conversion goals; they are not webhook events, which Kirora sends to you. Send each with an `Idempotency-Key` from your own event id, and keep event names fixed (a varying value belongs in `properties`), since a workspace holds at most 1,000 names. See [Events](/docs/api/events). A contact's events: `GET /v1/contacts/{id}/events`.

tags.name: lists
tags.description: A list is a fixed set of contacts you add and remove yourself; its membership changes only when you change it. Use a list for an audience you manage, a segment for one described by rules, and a tag to label campaigns and templates, not people. Adding contacts to a list can enroll them in a journey triggered by joining it. A contact's lists: `GET /v1/contacts/{id}/lists`.

tags.name: segments
tags.description: A segment is an audience described by rules, such as "ordered twice in 90 days", evaluated when it is used. Unlike a list, its membership changes as contacts and their events change, so a count or preview is true only for that moment. See [Objects and rules](/docs/api/models#segment-rules) for the rule grammar. A contact's segments: `GET /v1/contacts/{id}/segments`.

tags.name: topics
tags.description: A topic is a kind of marketing a contact can choose, such as product updates, and a topic choice is their choice for it on every channel or one. Topic choice works on top of consent, not instead of it: a send on a topic needs consent on the channel and the topic reaching the contact. An `opt_out` topic reaches everyone with consent who has not left it; an `opt_in` topic only those who joined. A contact's topic choices: `GET /v1/contacts/{id}/topics`.

tags.name: attributes
tags.description: Attributes are the custom fields your contacts carry, such as `plan` or `orders`, discovered from the values you send. These operations list the keys and their values for rule builders and merge tags; you set attributes on the contact itself, through `identify` or `updateContact`.

tags.name: tags
tags.description: A tag is a label on campaigns, journeys, segments and templates, such as "Black Friday", for filtering lists and reports. A tag is not an audience: to group contacts, use a list or a segment. A tag that a segment or journey rule names cannot be deleted until the rule stops naming it.

tags.name: transactional
tags.description: Transactional messages are one-off email or push sends to one recipient, such as receipts and password resets, that a person needs whatever their marketing choices. Transactional email ignores marketing consent and topics, but not a bounce or a transactional spam complaint. Transactional push still needs the contact's push consent and an eligible device. A send returns 202 when accepted, not when delivered: read each message in the message log (`GET /v1/messages/{id}`) for what happened. See [Transactional messages](/docs/api/transactional).

tags.name: campaigns
tags.description: A campaign is one marketing send to an audience, a list or a segment, at once or at a scheduled time. A campaign sends at most once; a journey is for messages that follow each contact over time. It reaches only contacts with consent on its channel, so check eligibility before sending. See [Campaigns and journeys](/docs/api/campaigns-and-journeys).

tags.name: journeys
tags.description: A journey is an automation that contacts enter on a trigger, such as an event or joining a list, and move through step by step over time. Where a campaign is one send to everyone at once, a journey sends to each contact when they reach each step. A live journey can be edited: the change reaches new entries, and a send step's content reaches everyone who has not reached the step yet. One an agent key wrote needs a person to confirm it before it goes live. See [Objects and rules](/docs/api/models#journey-definitions). A contact's journeys: `GET /v1/contacts/{id}/journeys`.

tags.name: conversion-goals
tags.description: A conversion goal says what counts as a result for a campaign or a journey: an event, such as an order, done within a window after one of its messages, with an event property summed as revenue. A journey's and a campaign's metrics report their goals; a journey can also end each enrollment when its goal is reached. Goals need a paid plan.

tags.name: templates
tags.description: A template is a reusable email design: a document of blocks and a theme, saved as a draft and published as numbered versions. Campaigns copy a template when they are built, so editing a template never changes a campaign already made from it. Send only from a published version; an agent key's edits wait for a person to publish them. See [Templates as code](/docs/api/templates-as-code).

tags.name: shared-blocks
tags.description: A shared block is a block kept once and placed in many templates, such as a footer or a product card. Editing one changes every draft that places it; a published template, a scheduled campaign and a live journey keep the copy they froze until they are published or saved again. Check its usage before changing it.

tags.name: assets
tags.description: An asset is an image you upload for a template's image blocks, served from a public URL. Anyone with the URL can see it, so never upload anything private.

tags.name: forms
tags.description: A form is a hosted sign-up, contact or waitlist form that creates or updates contacts and records the consent they give. Forms share a public link and can be embedded in your site; a submission returns 409 `FORM_CLOSED` once the form is closed by hand, by date or by its limit.

tags.name: messages
tags.description: The message log holds every message Kirora sent or tried to send, from campaigns, journeys and transactional sends, with what became of it. One send to one contact on one channel is one message, so a campaign to 1,000 contacts is 1,000 messages. Export the log as CSV for analysis. See [Message log and exports](/docs/api/messages). A contact's messages: `GET /v1/contacts/{id}/messages`.

tags.name: suppressions
tags.description: A suppression is a block on an email address, held whether or not a contact has it, with its reason. A bounce (`bounced`) or a spam complaint about a transactional message (`complained_transactional`) stops all email, transactional included. An unsubscribe (`unsubscribed`), a spam complaint about marketing mail (`complained`) and a block you add (`manual`, `imported`) stop marketing only: receipts, password resets and other transactional email still send.

tags.name: sending-domains
tags.description: A sending domain is a domain your email is sent from, with the DNS records that prove you own it. Nothing sends email from an address until its domain is verified here, and a domain can be verified in only one workspace, so use a subdomain for staging.

tags.name: senders
tags.description: A sender is a From address the workspace has saved, on one of its sending domains, with one default that new emails start with. List them to pick a From that can send; they are added and changed in the dashboard.

tags.name: push-projects
tags.description: A push project is a product whose iOS, Android and web apps receive push, with whether each can send. Push to a contact goes through their installations on a project that can send. See [Push notifications](/docs/api/push).

tags.name: webhooks
tags.description: A webhook is an endpoint of yours that receives Kirora's events, such as `message.delivered`. Each delivery is signed, and a failed one is retried on a schedule, up to eight attempts in all (see [Webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks#retries)). Verify each request's signature against the raw body before trusting it, and treat delivery as at least once and unordered. See [Webhooks](/docs/api/webhooks).

tags.name: reports
tags.description: Reports show how sending performs: the workspace overview, a comparison of campaigns, transactional delivery and conversion funnels. A report's window is counted by calendar day in the workspace's timezone, and a `to` date is exclusive.

tags.name: me
tags.description: These operations return the calling API key, its scopes and its workspace. Call `getMe` first to check that a key works and holds the scopes you need.

tags.name: workspaces
tags.description: Partner workspaces let a platform offer messaging to its own customers, one workspace per customer, created and run with a partner key and the `Kirora-Workspace` header. See [Choose an integration](/docs/api/integrations).

tags.name: embed-sessions
tags.description: Embed sessions let a partner's customers use Kirora's segment and email builders inside the partner's app for 15 minutes, without a key of their own. See [Choose an integration](/docs/api/integrations).

x-retry-kinds.key: Send `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key and body repeats nothing. Most writes replay the first response; a transactional send returns the message as it stands now.
x-retry-kinds.entries: Each entry carries its own `idempotencyKey`; a retried entry replays.
x-retry-kinds.state: Safe to retry: a repeat returns the current state, or 409 once it has moved on from it.
x-retry-kinds.converges: Safe to retry: a repeat sets the same values again.
x-retry-kinds.unique: A repeat after success is refused with 409 `ALREADY_EXISTS`: read the one the first created.
x-retry-kinds.done: A repeat after success returns 404 or 409: treat that as done.
x-retry-kinds.unsafe: A repeat without a key does it again; send `Idempotency-Key` and a retry within 24 hours replays the first response.

name.description: Unique within the workspace, ignoring case.
The new name; unique within the workspace, ignoring case.

targetTagId.description: The tag that takes over every item, and survives the merge.

operator.description: How to compare. Text comparisons (`equals`, `notEquals`, `contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `in`) ignore case and accents ("jose" matches "José"). `notEquals` and `notContains` also match contacts without the value. Date operators (`before`, `after`, `withinLastDays`, `moreThanDaysAgo`) compare as dates and times in UTC: a stored ISO-8601 date is the start of that day, `before` means earlier than the given day and `after` later than it, and a value that is not an ISO-8601 date or date and time never matches. `inNextDays` is a date from today to that many days ahead. `anniversaryInNextDays` (0 = today) and `anniversaryThisMonth` ignore the year, so they suit birthdays, and also read a yearless `--MM-DD`; a 29 February counts on 28 February in other years. Days are UTC days; these three are for attributes and dates, not contact fields.

value.description: What to compare with; its type depends on `operator`. Omit for `exists`, `notExists` and `anniversaryThisMonth`; an array of up to 100 for `in`; an ISO date for `before` and `after`; a number of days (up to 3650) for `withinLastDays`, `moreThanDaysAgo` and `inNextDays`, and 0 to 365 for `anniversaryInNextDays`.

field.description: The contact column to test. Each takes these operators, and is refused with others: `email`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `firstName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `lastName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `phone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `timezone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `externalId`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `consent.email`: equals; `consent.push`: equals; `country`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `locale`: equals, notEquals, startsWith, in, exists, notExists; `rfmGroup`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `purchaseCount`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `totalSpent`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `lastPurchasedAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo, exists, notExists; `createdAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo. `phone` holds +country numbers: write `equals`, `notEquals` and `in` values with their country code. Consent takes `true` or `false`. `purchaseCount`, `totalSpent` (in the main currency) and `lastPurchasedAt` are a customer's totals of the workspace's purchase event (`purchaseEvent` in workspace settings: an order, a paid invoice, a booking), recomputed daily with `rfmGroup`; the contact's stored `totalSpent` is null when the workspace's purchases carry no amount. In these comparisons a missing count or spend is 0, so someone who never purchased has 0 purchases and 0 spent.

operator.description: How to compare. Text comparisons (`equals`, `notEquals`, `contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `in`) ignore case and accents ("jose" matches "José"). `notEquals` and `notContains` also match contacts without the value. Date operators (`before`, `after`, `withinLastDays`, `moreThanDaysAgo`) compare as dates and times in UTC: a stored ISO-8601 date is the start of that day, `before` means earlier than the given day and `after` later than it, and a value that is not an ISO-8601 date or date and time never matches. `inNextDays` is a date from today to that many days ahead. `anniversaryInNextDays` (0 = today) and `anniversaryThisMonth` ignore the year, so they suit birthdays, and also read a yearless `--MM-DD`; a 29 February counts on 28 February in other years. Days are UTC days; these three are for attributes and dates, not contact fields.

value.description: What to compare with; its type depends on `operator`. Omit for `exists`, `notExists` and `anniversaryThisMonth`; an array of up to 100 for `in`; an ISO date for `before` and `after`; a number of days (up to 3650) for `withinLastDays`, `moreThanDaysAgo` and `inNextDays`, and 0 to 365 for `anniversaryInNextDays`.

operator.description: How to compare. Text comparisons (`equals`, `notEquals`, `contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `in`) ignore case and accents ("jose" matches "José"). `notEquals` and `notContains` also match contacts without the value. Date operators (`before`, `after`, `withinLastDays`, `moreThanDaysAgo`) compare as dates and times in UTC: a stored ISO-8601 date is the start of that day, `before` means earlier than the given day and `after` later than it, and a value that is not an ISO-8601 date or date and time never matches. `inNextDays` is a date from today to that many days ahead. `anniversaryInNextDays` (0 = today) and `anniversaryThisMonth` ignore the year, so they suit birthdays, and also read a yearless `--MM-DD`; a 29 February counts on 28 February in other years. Days are UTC days; these three are for attributes and dates, not contact fields.

value.description: What to compare with; its type depends on `operator`. Omit for `exists`, `notExists` and `anniversaryThisMonth`; an array of up to 100 for `in`; an ISO date for `before` and `after`; a number of days (up to 3650) for `withinLastDays`, `moreThanDaysAgo` and `inNextDays`, and 0 to 365 for `anniversaryInNextDays`.

field.description: The contact column to test. Each takes these operators, and is refused with others: `email`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `firstName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `lastName`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `phone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `timezone`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `externalId`: equals, notEquals, contains, startsWith, exists, notExists, in; `consent.email`: equals; `consent.push`: equals; `country`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `locale`: equals, notEquals, startsWith, in, exists, notExists; `rfmGroup`: equals, notEquals, in, exists, notExists; `purchaseCount`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `totalSpent`: equals, gt, gte, lt, lte; `lastPurchasedAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo, exists, notExists; `createdAt`: before, after, withinLastDays, moreThanDaysAgo. `phone` holds +country numbers: write `equals`, `notEquals` and `in` values with their country code. Consent takes `true` or `false`. `purchaseCount`, `totalSpent` (in the main currency) and `lastPurchasedAt` are a customer's totals of the workspace's purchase event (`purchaseEvent` in workspace settings: an order, a paid invoice, a booking), recomputed daily with `rfmGroup`; the contact's stored `totalSpent` is null when the workspace's purchases carry no amount. In these comparisons a missing count or spend is 0, so someone who never purchased has 0 purchases and 0 spent.

NOT_FOUND.description: No such resource in this workspace. Another workspace's resource returns the same.

METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED.description: The path exists, but not with this method. The `Allow` header lists the methods it takes.

PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE.description: The body, or an uploaded file, is larger than this route takes. `message` states the limit when the route sets its own.

UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE.description: The `Content-Type` is not one this route reads: send `application/json`, or `multipart/form-data` to an upload route.

RATE_LIMITED.description: Too many requests. Wait `Retry-After` seconds; `details.retryAfterSeconds` carries the same.

REVISION_CONFLICT.description: The template, campaign or journey changed since you read it (`expectedRevision` is stale). `details` carry the current `revision`, `updatedAt` and who changed it.

SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.description: A dependency is temporarily down. Retry with backoff.

UNAUTHORIZED.description: Key missing, malformed, revoked or expired.

VALIDATION_ERROR.description: Body, query, path or a header failed validation. `errors` lists each problem: `in` (`body`, `query`, `params`, `headers`, when known), `field` (dotted, empty for the whole part), `code` (when a schema rule failed), `message` (plain words, meant to be shown beside the field), and `minimum` or `maximum` on a `too_small` or `too_big` rule.

API_KEY_IP_NOT_ALLOWED.description: The key is restricted to other IP addresses.

AGENT_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.description: An agent wrote or edited this campaign or journey; a person confirms it in the dashboard before it sends, schedules or activates.

EMBED_BUILDER_UNAVAILABLE.description: This deployment does not serve the hosted builders yet, so no embed session can start. Retrying will not help.

EMBED_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED.description: 403: an embed session used from a page its partner key does not allow. 409: starting an embed session on a partner key with no `allowedOrigins`.

WORKSPACE_SUSPENDED.description: The workspace is suspended; nothing sends until it is resumed.

CONTACT_SEND_IN_PROGRESS.description: A message to this contact is being handed to a provider; retry in a few seconds.

EXPORT_UNAVAILABLE.description: 409: the export is not ready yet. 410: it has expired; start a new one.

NOTHING_TO_EXPORT.description: The export would hold no rows.

EVENT_NAME_LIMIT_REACHED.description: The workspace already tracks the most distinct event names it can. Delete unused names, and put what varies (ids, prices) in `properties`.

PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED.description: A limit of the workspace owner's plan stops this: emails this month or today, contacts, image storage, workspaces, members, sending domains, active journeys or the Kiro allowance. `details.entitlement` names the limit, `details.limit` and `details.used` say how far it goes, and `details.upgradeTo` names the plan that lifts it. A new account's daily email ramp returns the same way with `upgradeTo` null and `details.increasesAt`, when the ramp next raises the limit: no plan lifts it sooner.

PLAN_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE.description: The workspace owner's plan does not include this feature. `details.entitlement` names it and `details.upgradeTo` the plan that does.

CAMPAIGN_AUDIENCE_CONFLICT.description: Messages already exist for part of this audience from an interrupted send; send again to reconcile.

DRAFT_INCOMPLETE.description: The draft is not finished; `errors` names each missing or invalid field.

INVALID_SCHEDULE.description: A fixed `sendAt` is not in the future, or a local `localDateTime` has already passed in every timezone.

UNSUPPORTED_CHANNEL.description: The channel is not available on this deployment.

POSTAL_ADDRESS_MISSING.description: Marketing email needs the workspace's postal address; set it first.

CONSENT_MISSING.description: The contact has not consented on that channel.

SUPPRESSED.description: The address is suppressed on this channel, for any reason: a bounce, a spam complaint, an unsubscribe, an import or a block added by hand. A transactional send is refused only for a bounce or a complaint about a transactional message. `listSuppressions` shows the block and its `reason`.

TOPIC_UNSUBSCRIBED.description: The contact has unsubscribed from the campaign's or journey step's topic on that channel.

SIGNUP_BLOCKED.description: The address matches the workspace's signup blocklist, so no contact is created.

INVALID_SENDER_ADDRESS.description: The from-address is not a valid sender.

SENDING_DOMAIN_DMARC_MISSING.description: Marketing email needs a DMARC record on the sending domain (`p=none` at least).

SENDING_DOMAIN_IDENTITY_CONFLICT.description: The domain conflicts with an existing provider identity.

TEST_SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.description: The provider may or may not have accepted the test; check the inbox before retrying.

TEST_SEND_ROUTE_NOT_READY.description: The workspace's sending route is still being set up; retry the test in a few minutes.

TEST_SEND_UNAVAILABLE.description: The test could not be handed to the provider; retry shortly.

SENDING_DOMAIN_UNVERIFIED.description: The from-address is not on a verified sending domain; nothing sends from it until DNS verification succeeds.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE.description: A request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running; retry after a short wait to get its response.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.description: The first request with this `Idempotency-Key` failed or never returned, and may have taken effect (operations whose retry kind is `unsafe`): check, then retry with a new key.

CONTENT_NOT_RETAINED.description: The message exists, but what it sent was removed once sending finished, or has expired.

RECIPIENT_EMAIL_MISSING.description: The contact has no email address.

RECIPIENT_EMAIL_UNSUPPORTED.description: The contact's email address has non-ASCII characters before the @, which Kirora cannot deliver to yet.

TEMPLATE_NOT_PUBLISHED.description: `email.template` names a template with no published version. Publish it first.

TEMPLATE_ENVELOPE_INCOMPLETE.description: The template and the send together give no `subject` or no `from`; `details` name what is missing.

PUSH_DESTINATION_MISSING.description: The contact has no active push installation.

FORM_CLOSED.description: The form is closed: closed by hand, past its closing time, or at its submission limit. The message is the form's closed message.

errors.description: Each field the request got wrong: on `VALIDATION_ERROR` and `DRAFT_INCOMPLETE`.

details.description: What else the error carries, by `code`: see that code's description.

externalId.description: Your own id for the contact, as set with identify.

email.description: The contact's email address, matched trimmed and without case.

fontFamily.description: A font id: one every client has (arial, verdana, georgia, tahoma, times-new-roman, courier-new), or a web font, which shows where the client loads it and falls back to a safe font elsewhere. Form themes use the same ids.

mobileFontSize.description: Text size in px on phones (screens up to 620px), 12 to 72.

padding.description: Space inside the block in px, 0 to 100 per side; omitted sides keep their default.

borderWidth.description: Border thickness in px; 0 for none.

linkColor.description: Colour of links in the text.

linkUnderline.description: Set to false for links without an underline, such as a row of rating numbers or stars.

letterSpacing.description: Space between letters in px, such as 3 for a spaced-out eyebrow line.

textTransform.description: Set to `uppercase` to capitalise all text.

lineHeight.description: A multiple of the font size.

inset.description: Draw the background and border as a box within the content width, not across the whole row.

style.description: Visual overrides for this block, such as colours, font and spacing.

visibleIfPresent.description: Show the block only when this value is present (not missing, empty or false), such as `data.vat` for a VAT row; checked as each message is rendered.

showOn.description: Show the block only on phones (screens up to 620px) or only on wider screens. Clients that ignore screen size show the desktop version, and so does plain text. Omit to show it everywhere.

alt.description: The logo's alt text. Without `src`, it shows as a wordmark in the heading font; gallery samples set it to `{{ org.name }}`.

align.description: When unset, headings, text, buttons and boxed text start from the reading side (left, or right in a right-to-left language); other blocks centre.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: a repeat with the same key and body within 24 hours gets the first response again, with `Idempotency-Replay: true`. get.description:
Returns contacts in this workspace. To read one contact by its email address or your own id, use `GET /v1/contacts/{id}` with `idType`. `q` searches: it matches any part of the email address or name, ignoring case. `consent`, `suppressed`, `listId`, `segmentId`, `createdAfter` (inclusive) and `createdBefore` (exclusive) narrow the list and combine with each other and with `q`; an unknown list or segment is a 404. Each item is shaped like a single contact read: it carries its email suppression and the lists it is in (`listIds`). `meta.count` counts every contact matching the filters, up to 10000: beyond that it reports the cap and `meta.countExact` is `false`; both are counted on the first page only (null with a `cursor`). Results are newest first and cursor-paginated: pass `meta.pagination.nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it comes back `null`. The cursor is opaque — do not construct or parse one.

post.description:
Creates or updates a contact, matched by `externalId`, then `email`, then `phone` rather than by id, and created if none matches. A write whose lower-ranked identifier matches a contact that holds a different value for a higher-ranked one (a phone matching a contact with another email) names two people and is refused with 409 `CONFLICT`, `details.field` the identifier that differs. Consent flags that are omitted keep their current value rather than resetting to false. Granting consent, on a channel or (in `topics`) a topic, needs `consent.statement`, how the contact agreed; without it the write is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR` at `consent.statement`. Withdrawing needs none. `attributes` merge as on update: `null` removes a key. `topics` sets topic choices in the same write, each recorded in consent changes as `PUT /v1/contacts/{id}/topics/{topicId}` records it. `lists` adds the contact to lists by name, creating a list that does not exist yet; joining one starts any journey triggered by joining it. This is the endpoint to use for ingestion. Agent keys are refused with 403.

Requires API-key scope: `contacts:write`.

delete.description:
Deletes one contact and its data, for a right-to-erasure request: its events, list memberships, consent changes and journey enrollments go with it. Journey messages go with the enrollments; campaign and transactional messages are kept for campaign totals but anonymised: the address, content and provider ids are removed and nothing links them to the person. Address suppressions are kept, so a deleted address that is imported again is still not mailed. While a message to the contact is being handed to the provider, which takes seconds, it answers 409 `CONTACT_SEND_IN_PROGRESS`; retry shortly. A message waiting to be retried is skipped (`contact_deleted`) instead; a push that already reached one of the contact's devices is marked `sent`, and one a push service refused is marked `failed`, as it would have ended anyway. It cannot be undone. Requires `contacts:delete`; agent keys are refused.

Requires API-key scope: `contacts:delete`.

Deletes up to 100 contacts, each named by `contactId`, `externalId` or `email`, and reports an outcome per contact. For each one deleted, its events, list memberships, consent changes and journey enrollments go with it. Journey messages go with the enrollments; campaign and transactional messages are kept for campaign totals but anonymised: the address, content and provider ids are removed and nothing links them to the person. Address suppressions are kept, so a deleted address that is imported again is still not mailed. `send_in_progress` means a message was being handed to the provider; retry that one shortly. Requires `contacts:delete`; agent keys are refused.

Requires API-key scope: `contacts:delete`.

post.description:
Merges this contact, a duplicate, into the one `keep` names, for one person recorded twice. The kept contact keeps its values and gains any the duplicate had that it lacks: identifiers, name, timezone, country, locale, and attributes and dates by key. An email address or phone it gains brings that channel's consent with it; its own consent otherwise stands. The duplicate's messages, events, conversions, devices and consent changes move to the kept contact; its lists and suppressions are added, and its topic choices fill in topics the kept contact has not chosen. Then the duplicate is deleted, ending its journey enrollments. It cannot be undone. While a message to either is being handed to the provider, which takes seconds, it returns 409 `CONTACT_SEND_IN_PROGRESS`; retry shortly. A message waiting to be retried moves to the kept contact and still sends; the duplicate's copy of a campaign both received is skipped (`contact_deleted`) instead; a push that already reached one of the duplicate's devices is marked `sent`, and one a push service refused is marked `failed`, as it would have ended anyway. A `keep` that names no contact is a 404, and merging a contact into itself a 400 at `keep`.

Requires API-key scope: `contacts:write`.

post.description:
Records a behavioural event against a contact. Events drive journey triggers and segment rules, so this is the main ingestion endpoint for product activity. The event and its processing obligation are stored atomically: a 201 confirms storage, while journey and conversion effects run asynchronously afterwards. Name the contact by exactly one of `contactId`, `externalId` or `email`; a contact that does not exist is a 404, never created: identify it first. `occurredAt` defaults to now and may be at most 24 hours in the future; an event that arrives more than 72 hours after its `occurredAt` starts no journey, but still counts for history, exits and waits. Names are case-sensitive, up to 128 characters with no control characters, with leading and trailing spaces removed; those beginning with `contact.` are reserved for platform events. A workspace tracks at most 1,000 distinct names: a new one past that is refused with `EVENT_NAME_LIMIT_REACHED`, so keep ids and prices in `properties`. Send an `Idempotency-Key` from your own event id: without one, every request records a new event, so a retry after a timeout can record it twice and start a journey twice. A repeated `Idempotency-Key` with the same body returns the receipt first stored, with `Idempotency-Replay: true`; with a different body it is a 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. The body must be JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`). On the Free plan, which records only Kirora's own events, it is refused with 403 `PLAN_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE`.

Requires API-key scope: `events:write`.

The same key with another request is 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Use a new key, such as a UUID, for each new request.

Every event the workspace tracked, accepted or rejected, newest first: did an integration's event arrive, and if not, why? Accepted events are ordered and filtered by when they happened, rejected ones by when they arrived; the log reaches back `meta.retention`. A rejected event is a tracked event the API refused (validation, an unknown contact, the name limit, a deleted name), kept as sent with the error it answered; a batch refused whole is listed event by event. A request refused before its body was read (credentials, rate limit, plan, size, broken JSON) is not kept. `q` matches an event name exactly, or a contact's id, email address or external id (accepted events only: a rejected one has no contact); property values are not searched. Complete, not sampled. For a member, a property whose key is a masked attribute is left out, as on contact reads.

post.description:
Sends a one-off message to one recipient — a receipt, a password reset, a confirmation — bypassing campaigns. It ignores marketing preferences (it is the critical tier) but respects suppression. Agent keys are refused with 403.

**Channels.** Give `email`, `push`, or both. With both, `deliver: all` (the default) sends each one the contact can receive, and `deliver: first` sends push when the contact has a reachable device and email otherwise. A channel the contact cannot receive is passed over; only when none is left does the send fail, with that channel's reason. The response lists one message per channel sent.

**Data.** `data` holds the values the content reads as `{{ data.<key> }}`, once for every channel: a stored template, inline email, and the push `title` and `body`. Inline content (email or push) whose `{{ data.<key> }}` tag has no value in `data`, and no default, is refused with 400 rather than sent blank.

**Email.** Inline (`subject`, `from`, `html`, optional `text`, `previewText`, `replyTo`), or a stored template named by `template` (its alias, such as `password-reset`, or its id). The template's published version is rendered when the request is accepted and supplies the envelope; each envelope field given overrides it. The result needs a `subject` and a `from` (409 `TEMPLATE_ENVELOPE_INCOMPLETE`), and the `from` domain must be verified. A template never published is 409 `TEMPLATE_NOT_PUBLISHED`. Email is tracked only when `tracking` asks, and never for a contact in the EEA or the UK; `threading` continues a conversation. `attachments`, `threading` and `tracking` sit inside `email`.

**Push.** `push` takes the notification fields (`title`, `body`, `actionUrl`, …) beside `pushProjectId`, which is needed only when the workspace has several push projects.

**Recipient.** `to` names one `contactId`, `externalId` or `email`, and nothing else: set a contact's name or attributes with `POST /v1/contacts/identify` first. An `email` that matches no contact creates one for transactional mail only.

**Retries.** Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retry safe. A retry with the same key and request returns the first result, with `Idempotency-Replay: true`, and sends nothing again; the same key with a different request is 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Without a key, every request sends: a retry after a timeout can send the message twice. A replay answers from the messages as they are now, so its `status` can differ from the first answer, and an `externalId` or `email` recipient the first request created or updated stays so even when the send itself was refused. Set `correlationId` to your own reference: it is echoed on each message's webhooks and its read, and `GET /v1/messages?correlationId=` finds them. `sendAt` times the send, email and push alike.

Requires API-key scope: `transactional:send`.

get.description:
Splits a campaign's email results into rows by the recipient's email domain (`gmail.com`), the device they first opened or clicked on (`desktop`, `mobile`, `tablet`), or the contact's country (`NG`), counted the same way as the campaign's metrics. Use it to find where a problem sits: bounces concentrated on one domain point at that mailbox provider, not at the whole list.

Rows are ordered by messages sent, largest first. The 50 largest are listed, and everything past them is summed in `other` (null when there are none). A row's `key` is `null` when the value is unknown: a device is known only once a person opens with images on or clicks (Apple Mail Privacy Protection's automatic opens and Gmail's image proxy name no device, and other image proxies may read as desktop); a country only when the contact has one; a domain only while the message still names someone (not after the contact is deleted).

get.description:
Returns how a campaign's metrics built up over time: for each hour or day, how many messages were sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced and so on, with email and push counted apart. Use it to chart a send, for example to see that most opens came in the first six hours.

Each point counts what **happened** in that hour or day: an open at 10:05 counts in the 10:00 hour, whenever the email was sent. Opens and clicks count the first per message, as in the campaign's metrics. Because a point counts events, not the people sent to in that hour, don't divide one point by another to get an open rate; divide running totals.

The series starts at the campaign's first send and runs, with no gaps, to now, in the workspace's timezone (`timezone`). With `interval=hour` it covers at most 72 hours; with `interval=day`, at most 366 days. `from` and `to` narrow it (`from` inclusive, `to` exclusive, `from` before `to`); a date means the start of that day in the workspace's timezone. A campaign that has not sent yet, or a window ending before its first send, returns no points.

Requires API-key scope: `campaigns:read`.

Creates a multi-step automation in a draft state. A draft saves unfinished: it needs a name and a trigger, but may have no steps yet and send steps without their content; what is given is checked. Each step has an `id` you choose, unique within the journey, and transitions (`nextStep`, `onMatchStep`, `otherwiseStep`, split paths) name those ids: a step whose `nextStep` is omitted goes on to the next step in `steps`, `null` ends the journey there, and a branch's last step should set `null`. A transition to a step that does not exist, or one that leads back to a step already passed (a loop), is a 400 at that field. A journey does not run until it is activated, which needs it whole (409 `DRAFT_INCOMPLETE` lists each missing field in `errors`); edit it with `PATCH /v1/journeys/{id}`. An email step is built from its design (`templateSnapshot`): any `html` or `text` sent beside it is replaced by the design's rendering. A send step may set `onUnreachableStep` (the contact cannot receive the channel) and `onFailureStep`: taken when the message cannot be queued because the plan's sending allowance is used up (it is recorded `skipped`, reason `plan_limit_reached`). Delivery happens after the enrollment has moved on, so a later bounce or provider error does not branch. A contact enters one repeatable journey at most 10 times an hour, whatever its `waitAfterEntry`; past that, entries are skipped and the workspace admins are notified (`journey_loop_detected`).

Previews an enrollment without sending. `entry` says whether the contact would enter now: a date journey needs a valid date in its field; an event journey checks the supplied eventProperties against the trigger's conditions, then re-entry. The path follows branches on eventProperties and filters and splits on the contact as they are now; a wait-until step takes its match path. Each send step is checked against suppression, consent, topics and devices: `would_send`, `unreachable` (takes the fallback path), `failed` (the email allowance is used up and the step has `onFailureStep`) or `would_skip`, with the refusal code in `reason` (`DRAFT_INCOMPLETE` for a send step not yet finished: a draft simulates too; `PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED` when the email allowance is used up). An ended journey returns `journey_ended`; a draft or paused one is previewed as if live. A date journey enters only when its date is due now in the contact's timezone (`date_not_due` otherwise), once per occurrence; when due, its branches read the date occurrence instead of `eventProperties`. `maxEntries` and the hourly re-entry cap apply as they do live. post.description:
Sends the design in the request to one workspace member who has accepted their invitation; call once per recipient. Pass `contact` to render merge tags as that contact would see them. The test comes from `from`, or the workspace's default sender, on a verified sending domain: there is no shared sender, so a workspace sends tests once its own domain is verified (`SENDING_DOMAIN_UNVERIFIED` before then). Nothing is recorded as a message. An embed session may call this too: a session lets the chosen builders read what they need, render previews, count audiences, upload images and, when `testSendTo` lists addresses, send test emails to those addresses only. What each reason blocks:

| Reason | Marketing email | Transactional email | Sister workspaces | Deletable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `manual`, `imported` | Blocked | Sent | No | Yes |
| `unsubscribed` | Blocked | Sent | No | No: lifted when the person resubscribes |
| `complained` | Blocked | Sent | Marketing blocked | No |
| `bounced` | Blocked | Blocked | All email blocked | No |
| `complained_transactional` | Blocked | Blocked | All email blocked | No |

Sister workspaces are those with the same owner or partner. The list holds only this workspace's own blocks: an address blocked by a sister workspace's bounce is not listed here, yet every send to it is skipped. For the effective answer for one contact, read its `emailSuppression` (reason `other_workspace` for such a block).

Deletes a tenant workspace after a grace period. Partner keys only. Sending stops at once (403 `WORKSPACE_DELETION_PENDING`, queued messages skipped) and the status becomes `deleting`. Creates an embed session for one tenant. Partner keys only, from your server, with `Kirora-Workspace` naming the tenant. Returns a token the embedded segment and email builders send as `Authorization: Bearer es_…` for 15 minutes; the SDK asks your server for a new one before it expires. The key must have `allowedOrigins`, and a session is refused with 403 `EMBED_ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` from any other origin. A session lets the chosen builders read what they need, render previews, count audiences, upload images and, when `testSendTo` lists addresses, send test emails to those addresses only. It never saves, publishes or sends anything else; your server saves what the builders return. It sees masked attributes as a member does, and attribute values and event property samples only with `includeAttributeValues`. Revoking the key ends every session it minted. Use a new `Idempotency-Key` for each session: a repeat with the same key within 24 hours returns the first session again, whose token may have expired.
